instruction.text: Select each image to hear what the Windrush generation found when they arrived in Britain.

correct1.text: The buildings are so dismal and so old. There’s hardly anywhere to live because the Germans bombed Britain in the war.

correct2.text: Work is all over the place, but the jobs we are being offered are those that white workers aren’t too keen on taking — lowly paid positions or jobs where the work is hard.

correct3.text: It was alright at first, but now you have more and more people telling us to go back home.

correct4.text: Food is rationed in England, so there isn’t much to go round. It’s awfully different too, because in the West Indies things are highly seasoned, whereas English food is very plain.

atoms.b: Lots of people in the Windrush generation struggled to be ((++accepted annoyed)) in the UK.
Many of their qualifications were not accepted by certain ((++jobs bobs)).
Some landlords also refused to ((++rent run)) to them because of the colour of their skin.
Treating somebody unfairly because of the colour of their ((++skin wings)) is called racism.

trainers.hint: More than one answer can be correct.

atoms.a: What were the Windrush generation’s houses like?
What sort of jobs could the Windrush generation get?
Why might the Windrush generation have felt lonely or sad?

feedback.finish: Life was quite hard at times for the Windrush generation, but they managed to make homes in the UK nonetheless.

instruction.text: The Windrush generation also found lots of opportunities in the UK. Select the examples of businesses they opened.

trainers.feedback: Look around anywhere in the UK and you can see the Windrush generation’s influence!
